oil.summary: Crude markets suffered their worst single-day selloff in months on Friday, with WTI dropping 4.34% to $68.80/bbl and Brent falling 4.05% to $72.21/bbl, extending a punishing weekly loss of roughly 10% and a month-to-date collapse exceeding 22%. The dominant catalyst is a swift unwinding of the Hormuz risk premium: tanker traffic through the strait has rebounded sharply following a tentative Iran accord, and Saudi Arabia is expected to cut its August official selling prices to Asian buyers in response to crashing Middle East benchmarks. Demand headwinds compound the supply-side pressure — China's crude imports are tracking toward their weakest monthly level since 2016 at approximately 6.4 mb/d per Kpler, and Asian refiners have broadly pulled back from spot purchases. Additional bearish flow came from news that the US has temporarily eased Russian oil sanctions, opening a further potential supply channel. Options markets now price a 77% probability of an OPEC production increase at the next meeting.
drivers: Strait of Hormuz risk premium collapses as tanker traffic rebounds and Iran accord advances, triggering broad long liquidation
China crude imports on course for weakest month since 2016 at ~6.4 mb/d; broader Asian refiner spot buying also cooling
US temporarily eases Russian oil sanctions and Saudi Arabia expected to slash August OSPs, adding further supply-side pressure

gas.summary: Henry Hub natural gas edged down just 0.21% on the day to $3.336/MMBtu, but remains a relative outperformer with a 1-week gain of 3.19% and a 1-month gain of nearly 10%, in contrast to TTF's sharp monthly decline. The key bullish supply development is Ukraine's ongoing long-range drone campaign targeting Russian energy infrastructure: strikes hit a major Russian natural gas processing plant this week, and Kazakhstan has since cut output at the large Karachaganak field by approximately 25% as a result of damage to the Russian processing facility that handles its output. LNG supply lines are showing early signs of normalization, however, with reports of up to eight empty carriers massing at Qatar's Ras Laffan hub ready to load. TTF ticked up 0.61% on the day, though it remains 12.42% lower on the month, reflecting the partial easing of prior geopolitical tensions. SpaceX separately announced plans to begin construction next month on an eight-mile gas pipeline to support its operations.
drivers: Ukraine drone strikes on Russian gas infrastructure, including a major processing plant, have forced Kazakhstan to cut Karachaganak field output by ~25%
Henry Hub outperforms on a monthly basis (+9.74%), likely underpinned by supply disruption concerns, while TTF remains under pressure month-on-month (-12.42%)
LNG supply normalization signal: up to eight empty carriers reported at Qatar's Ras Laffan awaiting loading

power.summary: EU carbon (EUA) was largely unmoved on the day at $76.12/EUA (-0.31%), broadly stable on the week and up just 0.63% on the month, suggesting carbon markets are not yet pricing significant disruption from the geopolitical newsflow dominating oil and gas. The policy backdrop is constructive for renewables: the UK has joined eight other North Sea nations to advance offshore clean energy, and a DOE report cited potential for geothermal to power 65 million US homes by 2050. Power-sector demand dynamics are being shaped by the AI infrastructure build-out, with one analysis describing electricity as the scarcest commodity in the AI boom. TTF's mild daily uptick (+0.61%) is relevant for gas-fired power economics but the month-on-month decline of 12.42% continues to soften generation costs. News flow on Big Oil's retreat from green investment may weigh on longer-term capex sentiment for the sector.
drivers: EU EUA prices flat to marginally lower; near-term carbon market appears insulated from oil and gas geopolitical volatility
North Sea clean energy coalition expands to nine European nations; DOE geothermal report adds longer-term structural demand signal
AI-driven power demand framed as the dominant near-term growth driver for electricity consumption, intensifying grid investment urgency
